newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - FEB 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - FEB 6.

text.p: SLOVAKIA:
NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak parliament on Wednesday approved the creation of a committee to supervise the secret service, but failed to approve its members.
- The private sector accounted for 68.2 percent of the indistrial output and for 83.2 percent of construction in 1996.
- Commercial bank Istrobanka expects to post a net profit of around 100 millin crowns for 1996. The bank's balance sum totalled 21 billion crowns last year.
- The National Bank of Slovakia has still not approve the sale of the Slovak branch of Czech bank Agrobanka to a consortium of unnamed Slovak companies.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak parliament is expected to vote on a law on the creation of a state exim bank on Thursday.
- There are currently between 20 and 25 registered investment funds in Slovakia.
- State subsidies to for employment totalled 7.35 billion crowns in 1996. Some 4.29 billion went to the creation of new jobs.
- Slovakia's largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna has called an extraordinary shareholders' meeting for February 18. The agenda of the meeting includes changes to the company's statutes.
PRAVDA - The average wage in industry rose 8.4 percent year-on-year in 1996, while the increase in the construction sector was 10.1 percent. -- Bratislava Newsroomj, 42-7-521-8402
ROMANIA
Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Romania's economy is on the brink of collapse, the paper said.
- Romania's reform programme is back to square one, the paper said.
- The government decided to take a tough stand against companies which failed to pay their debts and taxes.
- Honeymoon between the state budget and farming sector is over, the paper said.
- The government might lose parliament's support if it implements unpopular measures, Transport Minister Traian Basescu says in interview.
ADEVARUL
- Bucharest's Romaero SA aircraft maker signed accord with Lockheed Martin Corp to open aircraft maintenance and repair centre.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The leu's stability could be achieved by controlling inflation, deficits and losses, the paper quotes central bank governor Mugur Isarescu as saying.
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc threatened to resign if the defence budget would be lower than 3.0 percent of the GDP, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The government tried to persuade international lenders to accept its plans to cut taxes on profit starting February.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Budget for social protection will amount to some 10 percent of the GDP, the paper said.
- Bucharest road traffic affected by large number of trucks.
General
ADEVARUL
- Miners' leader Miron Cosma told a Bucharest court he was not responsible for the 1991 riots which ousted Romania's first post-communist government.
- The National Liberal Party (Democratic Convention) will ask parliament to pass a bill allowing Romanians access to their former secret police files.
- Magistrates at the Bucharest municipal court continue strike, to protest against poor working conditions.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Police investigations showed that the Ukrainian vessel detained in the Danube port of Galati last week was laden with 27 tonnes of smuggled cigarettes.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Some 1,140 hectares of arable land in Insula Mare a Brailei were allegedly illegally distributed to senior members of the former ruling Party of Social Democracy, the paper said. ($=5,978)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264 REUTER
AUSTRIA:
VIENNA, Feb 6 (Reuter) - The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm's chief Claus Raidl is expected to become Creditanstalt's new boss, as he is Bank Austria's top candidate, which took over Creditanstalt at the beginning of the year.
- A joint holding of Bank Austria and Creditanstalt is planned to start on January 1, 1998.
- German baking giant Mueller will take over the majority of Austria's leading baker Ankerbrot.
- Economic research institute IHS says wages must be kept low, so that Austria's job market can improve in 1999.
DIE PRESSE
- Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel is strictly against plans to merge Bank Austria and Creditanstalt.

- Austrian oil group OMV's profits went up to a record high of 2.9 billion schillings in 1996. The dividend will be raised from 20 to 23 schillings. The company has shown interest in participation in provincial energy providers Begas, OKA and Ferngas.
- Brewer BBAG sets its hopes for growth on export. The company's sale of its Coca-Cola activities brought it profits of 500 million schillings. The dividend for 1996 is to remain constant.
- Austrians have not changed their travel, living and recreational habits due to the government's austerity measures. However expenditures on luxury goods and food are down.
KURIER
- Austria is losing its top position in trade with eastern Europe. This year even a trade deficit with that market is threatening the country, as the export industry is losing ground.
- Austria's economic growth was the lowest within the European Union in 1995.
- Austria's anonymous savings accounts have to be abolished within the next two months, otherwise the European Commission has threatened to take legal action against the country.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Fibremaker Lenzing is planning to take legal action against some of its European competitors, saying they were receiving illegal subsidies.
